Conceal

/kuhn-SEEL/ - rhymes with reveal · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Conceal means to hide something from view or keep it from being known.

Maya concealed her disappointment behind a bright smile as the winner's name was read aloud.

Worked Example

A pitcher spends years learning to conceal his grip: the ball stays buried in the glove until the last instant, because a batter who glimpses the fingers knows what pitch is coming. Nothing about the hiding is against the rules—but it must be complete.

Conceal is stronger and more purposeful than 'hide' or 'cover': it implies careful effort to keep something from being seen or known at all, which is why the glove, the angle, and the timing all matter.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

hide: the everyday word; conceal adds purposeful care in the hiding

mask: to cover something with a layer that changes how it appears

cloak: to wrap something so fully that its shape disappears—often used of non-physical things

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

reveal: to bring something into view or into the open

expose: to uncover something, often wrongdoing, against its keeper's wishes

Where it sits · how completely it is put beyond finding — cover → conceal → erase

cover vs. conceal: Covering something merely puts a layer over it—a tarp over a bike says nothing about secrecy—while concealing means working to keep it from being found.

erase vs. conceal: Erasing goes further than concealing: a concealed diary still exists for someone to discover, but an erased file is gone, with nothing left to find.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: thoroughly (an intensifier)

Root — ceal

Root — ceal: to hide (from Latin celare)

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (thoroughly) + ceal (to hide) = to hide thoroughly. Latin celare, 'to hide,' is the quiet ancestor here; the prefix simply turns the volume up. English almost never uses the bare root on its own, so conceal carries the family's whole meaning: hiding done completely and on purpose.

Use the root in a new word: occult

Use the root in a new word: occult: Astronomers say the moon occults a star when it slides in front and hides the star from view.

Word Choice

neutral

Conceal is the act of hiding a particular thing—a key, a fact, a feeling—done with some care. A person whose whole habit is hiding is secretive, and an action carried out so no one notices is surreptitious; both are words in this unit. Reach for conceal when the focus is on the thing kept out of sight, and for disclose, its opposite here, when the thing is finally brought into the open.
